records.name: Journal of Machine Learning Research
records.scope_notes: Machine learning theory, algorithms, analysis and methodological insight. Routine applications of ML to other domains are excluded. Unsolicited surveys are not considered; separate open-source-software guidance applies.

route.conditions: The author page explicitly rules out publication fees. It describes the submission workflow but does not explicitly rule out a submission fee; retain pending independent fee audit. Surveys are invitation-only and current originality guidance also states that review articles are not published.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No publication fees stated; a separate explicit submission-fee statement was not located.

fee_evidence.note: The journal explicitly states that there are no publication fees and published papers are freely available. Submission-fee absence is not separately explicit on this page.

difficulty.basis: Discovery has not established an acceptance-difficulty ranking; fee-free status does not imply easy acceptance.

records.name: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research

route.conditions: No submission or publication charges. Surveys have separate guidelines. Standard journal submission does not require conference participation.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the no-author-fee policy for the standard journal route.

fee_evidence.note: The FAQ explicitly states that authors are not charged for submitting or publishing articles.

records.name: Transactions on Machine Learning Research
records.publisher: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (self-published; part of Journal of Machine Learning Research Inc.)
records.scope_notes: Original ML research, theoretical or empirical studies, reproducibility studies, and applications that reveal strengths or weaknesses of methods. The current FAQ excludes survey papers as of September 1, 2026.

route.conditions: No fees or payments imposed on authors. Per-author annual submission quotas apply. Expanded archival conference papers are excluded. Journal-to-conference presentation opportunities are separate from journal publication and any attendance costs.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the no-author-fee policy for the standard journal route.

records.name: Journal of Open Source Software
records.scope_notes: Peer-reviewed papers about mature open research software across disciplines. Excludes pre-trained ML models, notebooks, thin API clients and one-off analysis tools; does not publish a research-results article in place of a software paper.

route.conditions: No submission or publication fees. Software needs an OSI-approved license, demonstrated research use, tests and documentation, and more than six months of public iterative development. Review and required archive release are public. AI assistance requires disclosure and human responsibility.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the no-author-fee policy for the standard journal route.

fee_evidence.note: The current submission guide explicitly states that submitting and publishing in JOSS carry no fees.

difficulty.basis: Discovery has not established an acceptance-difficulty ranking; fee-free status does not imply easy acceptance.

records.name: Journal of Statistical Software
records.scope_notes: Substantial open-source statistical software and reproducible articles, including smaller code snippets. Methods innovations should be published elsewhere first; a JSS implementation needs its own substantial software contribution.

route.conditions: Free submission and no author fees. Requires GPL or GPL-compatible software, manuscript source, and replication material reproducing all results. Authors prepare the final publishable files. No page or figure limit is stated, although long articles can take longer to review.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the no-author-fee policy for the standard journal route.

fee_evidence.note: The journal explicitly describes free submission and states that it charges no author fees or subscription fees; manuscript preparation has no page or figure limit.

records.name: Logical Methods in Computer Science
records.publisher: Logical Methods in Computer Science e.V.
records.scope_notes: Theoretical and practical computer science involving logical methods, including formal reasoning, proof, semantics and verification. Original research and surveys are in scope.

route.conditions: Free Episciences overlay-journal route. Authors must first deposit the paper and TeX source in arXiv/CoRR with cs.LO included, then submit through Episciences. Normally at most 50 pages unless justified to the handling editor. Repository moderation remains distinct from journal peer review.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated in the no-author-fee policy for the standard journal route.

fee_evidence.note: The platform policy applies to all Episciences journals and says submission and publication are not conditional on payment; there are no access or publication fees.

notes: Ten credible journal candidates span AI/ML, formal computer science, software engineering, research software, graph/data research and information systems. Nine have verified free standard routes at discovery; JMLR remains needs_verification solely because no separate explicit submission-fee statement was located.

Official journal or publisher policy pages were opened live. Search snippets were used to find leads, not as the sole basis for a verified-free fee conclusion. The JOT author page intermittently timed out; its live submission-system page supplied current scope and its accessible homepage supplied fees.

No ACM venue is assumed free after the 2026 open-access transition; no IEEE venue is inferred free from optional OA alone. Conference registration and presentation are not included in these journal-route conclusions.
Information Research was considered but omitted because key current policy pages returned an anti-bot access-denied page; it may be worth a separate expansion audit.

Current restrictions retained: TMLR FAQ excludes surveys from 2026-09-01; JOSS current documentation requires more than six months of public iterative development and demonstrated research use. Older Open Journals documentation is not the controlling JOSS scope source.

Ranking evidence lead for the ranking role: JAIR's official transparent-publishing page reports 2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01 evaluation statistics released on 2026-04-16, including modeled acceptance quantities whose denominators and resubmission treatment need careful interpretation. No metrics were copied into discovery records.

Independent agent fee/ranking/reviewer work remains separate from this discovery pass and from human scientific review. A zero-fee route does not waive scope, originality, artifact, ethical, licensing, or peer-review requirements.
